title: Pith review finding
description: A finding from a Phase 6 (Verification) adversarial review of the clean-room rebuild, or an array of findings (one reviewer's output). A reviewer for one dimension fills id to fix. A separate verifier for the same dimension, who must try to reproduce the finding, fills verifier. Findings are ranked by severity, fixed, then re-checked on the real-file harness.

id.description: Unique within the review, e.g. round, dimension and number.

round.description: Which review round produced this finding.

dimension.description: The review dimension the reviewer was assigned.

severity.description: high: data loss, wrong output that looks right, a hang or crash, a privacy leak, or a broken must-have requirement. medium: wrong or degraded behaviour with a workaround, or in an uncommon path. low: polish, clarity or minor inefficiency.

line.description: 1-based line the finding anchors to, or null when it isn't tied to one line.

title.description: The defect in one short line.

scenario.description: Concrete inputs and state that lead to the wrong output, hang or crash, precise enough for the verifier to reproduce.

reviewer.description: Which agent or session reported it.

status.description: Where the finding stands. A fixed finding needs a confirmed or plausible verifier verdict and a recheck. A refuted finding is usually closed as not-a-bug.

verdict.description: confirmed: the verifier reproduced it. plausible: not reproduced, but the reasoning holds against the code. refuted: shown not to happen, or not to be a defect.

evidence.description: What the verifier did and saw: the test or command run and its output, or the code path that rules the finding out.

reproducedWith.description: The test, harness run or command used to reproduce it.

verifiedBy.description: Which agent or session verified it. Not the reviewer who reported it.

result.description: Whether the fix held when re-checked.

evidence.description: How the fix was re-checked, e.g. the self-tests and the end-to-end harness on real files, run several times.

examples.title: waitUntilExit() can hang when called off the launching thread
examples.scenario: Start a conversion from a background queue. The child process exits, but Process.waitUntilExit() never returns, so the job stays 'running'. It shows only under some timings, so run the harness several times.
examples.fix: Wait on terminationHandler (for example, resume a continuation from it) instead of calling waitUntilExit().

verifier.evidence: Reproduced by repeating the end-to-end harness with jobs started off the main thread; not reproduced after the fix.

recheck.evidence: Self-tests and the end-to-end harness on real files pass across repeated runs.

examples.title: Temporary files may be left behind when a job is cancelled
examples.scenario: Cancel a video conversion halfway through; its partial output stays in the temporary folder.
examples.fix: Delete the temporary output in the cancel path.

verifier.evidence: Cancelled jobs at several points and listed the temporary folder after each; nothing remained. The cleanup already runs on every exit path.
